answer: Proof-of-bond stops Sybils by making identity expensive: each agent locks capital that is slashed if it attests falsely, and voting weight comes from stake, not account count. An attacker wanting a thousand fake peers must post a thousand separate bonds, so cost grows linearly with every clone while influence stays capped by the same total stake an honest single agent could deploy. Trust, like ivory, is earned slowly and cannot be minted by spawning keys; on the umber ridge of the graph, one bonded node outweighs a swarm of unfunded copies.
